newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks stumble on heavy profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks stumble on heavy profit-taking.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed sharply off for the second session running in thin trade as profit-taking after a recent rally undermined key stocks including power giant Endesa, said traders.
"Some stocks, especially the most liquid like Endesa, have got a bit ahead of themselves as investors wanted Chilean exposure," said one dealer.
The bearish mood is seen continuing at the opening, although the fall should be less than today's, he added.
The 40-share IPSA index closed down 1.29 percent at 134.39 points.
The general IGPA index declined 0.77 percent to 5,798.52 points amid turnover of 9.46 billion pesos.
Traders said the bourse, which reached a year high point Thursday, could remain sluggish for weeks as investors speculate that Central Bank could soon trim interest rates again, said dealers.
"But personally, I think the Central Bank is unlikely to do anything til August," added one trader.
The bank's surprise move to cut rates 10 days ago together with heavy rains ending this year's drought sparked the bolsa to rally to new heights last week.
Telecom CTC retreated on a downgrade from Lehman Brothers to hold from buy on concerns of overvaluation after recent sharp rise in its stock price, said traders.
CTC, Chile's largest telecom carrier, ended down 1.36 percent at 3,640 pesos.
Other decliners included Endesa, down 2.34 percent at 312-1/2 pesos, and Copec, which shed 1.25 percent at 1,970 pesos.
Winners included forestry firm Infodema, up five percent at 21 pesos, and drug-maker LabChile, which rose 0.37 percent to 537 pesos. ((-- Margaret Orgill, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595 x212))
